text.p: These are the leading stories of Albania's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters does not vouch for the accuracy of these stories.
KOHA JONE
- The left smashes Berisha, runs the paper's headline.
- After five years of domination, the Democratic Party no longer rules the country and Sali Berisha ceased being Albania's absolute leader.

- The Socialist Party has won 60 constituencies on June 29 elections, the Democratic Party won seven whereas a rightist coalition, the Democratic Alliance Party and the ethnic Greeks failed to achieve what they expected.
- President Sali Berisha is on the verge of resigning.
- The OSCE said Albania's elections were acceptable.
- Deputy Interior Minister Agim Shehu and the head of the Republican Guard, Xhahid Xhaferri, have left the country.
- Genc Pollo, the Democratic Party's secretary general, has not won in his eastern constituency of Korce.
- The real star on election day was Albanian police which performed its duty according to the law. The paper said the role of police gave Tirana its normality back.
ALBANIA

- Albanians have returned the king to power, the daily's headline said, publishing pictures of communist dictator Enver Hoxha and Leka Zogu, who wants the restoration of the monarchy his father built in 1928.
- The Socialist Party won by force of arms. A Socialist Party backer killed the chairman of the Democratic Party in Fieri region village on election day.

- An analyst of Toronto University said Albania needed more time to carry out its process of national reconciliation and the elections were held earlier because the international community wanted to wash it hands of the crisis.

- A representative of the British Helsinki Committee said the elections were not satisfactory, his organisation had seen a more open electoral process last year but last Sunday's elections marked progress in several directions.
- The dollar fell slightly to 179 leks on Monday from 180 leks on Sunday after the holding of general parliamentary elections.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- The Socialist Party has scored a big victory by winning over 55 percent of the vote, the paper claimed. They said they will have 85 MPs in the 155-seat parliament.
- The result of the referendum over whether to change the republic into a monarchy is still a mystery. An aide to exiled king Leka claimed they had won 60 percent but the vote was being manipulated.
- The Socialist Party have won many seats in the capital Tirana.
Transmission was aborted
